report.summary: Reviewed chunk 6 of daedalus/mapping/drift.py: acceptance/ignore drift handling, refresh, main CLI. Claims mostly kept; one docstring claim about fail-closed init is kept.

handoff.purpose: Finalize drift report with ignore/acceptance handling, refresh, and CLI entry.

symbols.name: refresh
symbols.note: Re-baselines snapshot; carries acceptances forward verbatim.

claims.text: An ABSENT key reads as "nothing was excluded", not as "do not check". Deleting the field must not be a quieter way to narrow the run than setting the variable was.
claims.why: old_ignore defaults to {"env": "", "file": ""} when not a dict, and IGNORE_DRIFT is emitted when old_ignore != new_ignore, so absent/deleted field yields empty ignore and drift is detected.

claims.text: Only ACCEPTABLE_KINDS count as a match. An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news.
claims.why: by_key only collects items whose kind is in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS; if an acceptance matches such item, it is marked accepted; if not matched, STALE_ACCEPTANCE is emitted.

claims.text: An acceptance ... must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news.
claims.why: If no matched items (because the item is now reached and kind not acceptable), STALE_ACCEPTANCE is added.

claims.text: Acceptances are carried forward verbatim -- refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason.
claims.why: refresh loads old snapshot, parses acceptances, and passes them to write_snapshot unchanged.

claims.text: CI gate, not a pre-commit hook: it parses the whole tree and takes seconds.
claims.why: main calls check which calls scan (parses whole tree); no pre-commit hook mechanism is present.

claims.text: a missing snapshot fails, so deleting it is never a green run
claims.why: In default path, check is called without write_missing; missing snapshot causes first_run True and main returns 1 (fail closed).

claims.text: Fail CLOSED, matching `daedalus map --check`. This used to write the baseline and exit 0, which made `rm docs/architecture-state.json` a green run through a door reach.py itself classifies as an entry point.
claims.why: When report.first_run is True, main returns 1 without writing baseline, so missing snapshot fails closed.

claims.text: An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news.
claims.why: If item kind is now acceptable and accepted, it is marked accepted; if not, STALE_ACCEPTANCE is emitted.

claims.text: A run that looks at less of the tree than the baseline did cannot be compared with it, and a green result from one must never be indistinguishable from a green result from the other
claims.why: When old_ignore != new_ignore, IGNORE_DRIFT is added; this makes the result non-green (blocking) so green results are distinguishable.
